whyBeyou.title: Why Beyou?
whyBeyou.paragraph: I've always had trouble keeping my tasks organized. I also wanted to see if I was progressing in certain areas of my life. For every app I tested, only one of those things was there. So I started building my own personal habit and routine organization app, more to learn programming, but also to ultimately have the product I always wanted, where I can easily create habits and tasks with life categories and see the evolution over time, not to mention the ease of creating customized daily routines and goals to always stay on track.

localExecution.title: How to execute the project locally
localExecution.description: Everything below runs on your machine with just Git and Docker (Compose v2). The containers compile and run the whole stack, so you never install Java or Node on the host.

createFolder.title: Create a dedicated folder
createFolder.description: Create a folder where all the projects will live, e.g. a 'beyou' folder. The dev stack builds the backend and frontend from sibling directories, so the layout matters.

cloneRepos.title: Clone the repositories side by side
cloneRepos.description: Clone the dev-environment orchestrator together with the backend and frontend, all into the same folder:
cloneRepos.code:
git clone https://github.com/AndDev741/Beyou-dev-env.git
git clone https://github.com/AndDev741/Beyou-backend-spring.git
git clone https://github.com/AndDev741/Beyou-Frontend.git

createEnvFile.title: Create the .env file
createEnvFile.description: Inside Beyou-dev-env, copy .env.example to .env. Every variable is documented in the file itself; at minimum, set TOKEN_SECRET (32+ random characters) and a real Postgres password. There is also a table explaining each variable at the end of this topic.

runScripts.title: Run the stack
runScripts.description: Dev mode builds your local clones and hot-reloads them as you edit. The first boot takes a few minutes because everything compiles into named volumes; later starts reuse them. Production-like mode ignores your clones entirely: it pulls the images CI publishes to GitHub Container Registry, runs them detached behind nginx, and lets Watchtower redeploy each time a new image is pushed. Once the stack is up, open http://localhost:3000 (the API answers on http://localhost:8099/api/v1).
runScripts.devLabel: Development: hot reload from your local clones
runScripts.prodLabel: Production-like: published GHCR images, kept fresh by Watchtower

scriptsExplanation.title: What each script does
scriptsExplanation.upDev: up-dev.sh – builds backend and frontend from your sibling checkouts and runs the stack in the foreground with hot reload.
scriptsExplanation.upProd: up-prod.sh – pulls the published ghcr.io/anddev741/beyou-* images and runs the production-like stack detached; nginx serves the web build and Watchtower redeploys on new images.
scriptsExplanation.down: down.sh – stops the stack and removes orphans (pass 'dev' or 'prod' mode).
scriptsExplanation.resetDb: reset-db.sh – tears down the dev stack and deletes the Postgres volume. Irreversible.
scriptsExplanation.monitoring: --monitoring – optional flag for up-dev.sh, up-prod.sh and down.sh; adds the observability overlay (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, GlitchTip).

envExplanation.title: Environment variables (.env)
envExplanation.description: These are the variables you'll touch first; .env.example documents every one of them inline:
envExplanation.postgresDb: POSTGRES_DB – name of the database (default: beyou).
envExplanation.postgresPassword: POSTGRES_PASSWORD – database password. The template ships it empty on purpose: set your own long, random value.
envExplanation.postgresPort: POSTGRES_PORT – host port where PostgreSQL is exposed (default: 5490).
envExplanation.tokenSecret: TOKEN_SECRET – secret used to sign JWT tokens; 32+ characters of randomness.
envExplanation.googleClientId: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID – OAuth 2.0 client ID for Google sign-in; leave empty to disable.
envExplanation.cookieSecure: COOKIE_SECURE – set to 'true' for HTTPS, 'false' for local development.
envExplanation.corsAllowedPattern: CORS_ALLOWED_PATTERN – allowed CORS origin pattern. '*' works in dev; the prod profile refuses a wildcard.
envExplanation.mailSettings: MAIL_* (optional) – SMTP credentials for the verification and password-reset e-mails.
envExplanation.frontendUrl: FRONTEND_URL – URL of the frontend (default: http://localhost:3000/).
envExplanation.docsImportSettings: DOCS_IMPORT_* – source repo and secret for the documentation import that feeds this site.
envExplanation.monitoringVars: GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD, GLITCHTIP_* – required only with --monitoring; they have no defaults on purpose.

collaboration.description: Beyou is open-source under the Apache 2.0 license. Contributions are welcome — here's how to get involved.

repos.title: Project Repositories
repos.description: The project is spread across 6 repositories on GitHub, all under AndDev741:
repos.frontend: Beyou-Frontend — Monorepo: the React web app (apps/web), the native mobile app in React Native + Expo (apps/mobile), shared packages, and the marketing site
repos.backend: Beyou-backend-spring — Spring Boot API (auth, domain logic, persistence)
repos.devEnv: Beyou-dev-env — Docker Compose orchestration: dev with hot reload, production from published images, and the monitoring overlay
repos.e2eTests: Beyou-e2e-tests — Playwright end-to-end suite that drives the full stack (frontend, backend, and Postgres together)

monitoring.title: Monitoring & Observability
monitoring.description: Beyou ships its observability as a single Compose overlay (docker-compose.monitoring.yml). It is the same file in development and in production, so what you debug locally is exactly what runs deployed.

prometheus.name: Prometheus
prometheus.question: How is it performing?
prometheus.description: Scrapes the backend's /actuator/prometheus plus cAdvisor, node-exporter and postgres-exporter: JVM internals, per-container resources, the host, and the database's own view of itself.

loki.name: Loki + Alloy
loki.question: What happened?
loki.description: The apps need no log configuration at all. Alloy tails the stdout of every beyou* container through the Docker API and pushes to Loki, which works out log levels on the server side. Logs are kept for 30 days.

glitchtip.name: GlitchTip
glitchtip.question: What broke?
glitchtip.description: Sentry-compatible error tracking: backend, web, and mobile all report to it by DSN. It also owns the uptime and heartbeat monitors, since it is the piece that can actually notify a human.

monitoring.grafana: All three surface in one Grafana (localhost:3001), with four dashboards provisioned automatically: Containers (fleet health), Service Health (backend JVM), AI Agent, and Logs.
monitoring.how: Add the flag to the up and down scripts. Before the first run, set GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD, GLITCHTIP_SECRET_KEY and GLITCHTIP_DB_PASSWORD in .env. They have no defaults on purpose.

notes.title: Worth knowing
notes.sameFile: One overlay file serves every environment, so the monitoring you test in dev is the same monitoring that runs in prod.
notes.zeroConfig: Log collection is scoped to Compose projects whose name starts with 'beyou'. Deploy from a directory named differently and logs silently stop flowing.
notes.loopback: Every admin surface binds to 127.0.0.1 only (Grafana 3001, Prometheus 9090, GlitchTip 8000). Loki gets no host port at all: its unauthenticated API is reachable only through Grafana. Use a tunnel or reverse proxy, never a wider binding.
notes.firstRun: GlitchTip lets the first account to register become admin. Register yours right after the first boot, while port 8000 is still loopback-only.
notes.bootstrap: ./scripts/bootstrap-glitchtip.sh then creates the GlitchTip org, projects, uptime monitors, and alert rules. Registration stays manual on purpose: a bootstrap script has no business holding your password.
